APP COINAGE — the app itself, framed as a restricted collection of case files. Atmospheric register: it appears in titles, errors and empty states, never on a button. Pick one word per language and use it everywhere; it is the central metaphor. Avoid a word meaning a mere computer backup.

APP COINAGE — a saved game. The user's list of them is the "Case files" screen. Never "saved game", "session", "slot" or "match". Keep the archive metaphor: this is a paper file about an investigation.
APP COINAGE for a play session, distinct from the rules term "investigation phase". Starting a game is "begin an investigation". Never "create game" or "new session".
APP COINAGE — a deck of cards, framed as a folder of papers. Never "deck" or "collection" in the UI, though the rules term for a deck stays intact on cards themselves.
APP COINAGE — the user. Someone admitted to read the archive, never its owner. The copy never calls them a reader, a player or a scholar.
APP COINAGE — the archive's gatekeeper, the voice that refuses. Failures and limits speak as the desk rather than as software: "the desk declines", not "permission denied".
APP COINAGE — having an account, framed as being admitted to the archive rather than owning a profile. Never "account" in the SaaS sense, and never a supernatural pact or binding.
APP COINAGE — an anonymous account: no credentials taken, no record kept, this device alone. Keep it concrete and paper-like.
APP COINAGE — a registered account: credentials given once, good from any device. Contrast with visitor's ticket.
APP COINAGE for email, name and password together. Never "personal information", "particulars" or "details".
APP COINAGE for registering an account. Never "sign up" or "create account". British spelling in the English source.
Operative register, plain and short. Never "log in" or "log on". Use whatever a native speaker expects on an authentication button in your language.
